title.english: Hind bint Sahl ibn 'Amr ibn Jashm, the Ansari woman of Banu Jashm. She embraced Islam and pledged allegiance.

segments.arabic:
١١٨٥٨- هند بنت سهل
بن عمرو بن جشم الأنصاريّة الجشميّة، أسلمت وبايعت.
(١) الثقات ٣/ ٤٣٩.
(٢) أسد الغابة ت (٧٣٤٨) .
segments.english:
11858—Hind bint Sahl ibn 'Amr ibn Jashm, the Ansari woman of Banu Jashm. She embraced Islam and pledged allegiance.

¹ al-Thiqat, 3/439.

² Usd al-Ghaba, entry 7348.

segments.arabic: قاله الواقديّ فيما حكاه ابن سعد.
segments.english: This was stated by al-Waqidi, as Ibn Sa'd related from him.

unresolved.arabic_span: هي والدة الحارث بن أوس بن معاذ ... فولدت له الحارث بن أسلم
unresolved.explanation: The two reports identify Hind's son as al-Harith ibn Aws ibn Mu'adh and al-Harith ibn Aslam respectively. The Urdu witness preserves both readings, while the collateral Usd al-Ghaba passage confirms only the first. The canonical wording has therefore been translated literally without silently merging or emending the identities.

unresolved.arabic_span: أمها أم جندب بنت رفاعة أم زنبر بن زيد بن مالك الأوسية
unresolved.explanation: The wording has been rendered literally as identifying Umm Jundab as the mother of Zanbar ibn Zayd ibn Malik. The supplied witnesses do not determine whether the transmitted maternal genealogy is historically sound or corrupt.
